term: rigid identity versus strict sentence co-reference
resolution: RigidAt constrains which bearer a name can denote along M edges and ties denotation to existence; CoRef requires a shared denotation at a description. The theorem therefore distinguishes conditional identity wherever the bearer exists from Box of strict CoRef, which additionally requires NecessaryAt. It never infers necessary existence from rigid naming. E-only descriptions may vary reference; absence of E-necessity is modeled admission uncertainty, not proven ignorance, conceivability or an a posteriori discovery. No historical interpretation is asserted.
